correctness.rationale: For a common three-value alphabet of strict common-sign mixed items, every unequal valuation pair uses the same ordered magnitude pair u>v of one sign; equal totals imply the two orientations occur equally often. Each item goes to a highest valuer, establishing global welfare optimality. The welfare-optimal directed items supply equal nonnegative envy slack for both agents. A signed common-item balancing rule has a proved induction: if its sum difference is nonzero, a helpful item on the relevant side has magnitude at least the absolute difference. Each envy gap is the signed difference minus slack, so one permitted item removal suffices. Proof covers arbitrary real valuations and all finite lengths; standalone exact-integer verifier checks 117995 eligible exhaustive profiles, 3186 independent fair-optimum brute-force profiles, 13555 seeded eligible randomized profiles, and six four-value witnesses. Finite tests are supplementary, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The most relevant primary theorem (Teh 2026, arXiv:2609.01580 Thm 3.8) establishes a four-value unbounded counterexample but does not supply the positive zero-welfare-loss three-nonzero-value theorem. A 2020 ternary result does establish utility-maximizing EF1 for a different alphabet {-a,0,b}, so the new claim is explicitly confined to strictly nonzero three-valued common-sign alphabets with two levels of one sign. Its signed balancing argument handles heterogeneous same-sign utilities that are absent in that earlier domain. Searches of synonyms, dual signs, and broad EF1+PO statements, plus private previous claims, did not reveal an implication covering this theorem. Priority remains subject to unindexed literature.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier equivalent theorem or a reduction from a broader unpublished mixed-manna result could undermine priority; searches do not prove uniqueness.

value.rationale: Motivated by Teh 2026 Section 3.6, which proves unbounded EF1 utilitarian welfare price even under common signs and equal totals with four singleton values. The result supplies the exact sharp three-to-four alphabet cardinality boundary, giving zero loss for every strict mixed-sign three-valued profile and unbounded loss with four. The proof reveals the structural reason via a unique signed heterogeneous pair and balanced orientations, and yields a linear-arithmetic-time constructive rule. This is neither a fixed-size census nor a restatement of EF1+PO existence.
